title: macOS Filesystem Capacity from Splunk TA df
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'macOS Filesystem Capacity from Splunk TA df' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `linux_capacity_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `linux_macos_filesystem_capacity_from_splunk_ta_df` (UC-1.1.134), SOC dashboard panel "Linux — macOS Filesystem Capacity from Splunk TA df", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:linux_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=os` sourcetype='df' where `entity` satisfies `use_pct` > 90 for UC-1.1.134 ('macOS Filesystem Capacity from Splunk TA df'). Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `os` / `df` events where `entity` stays below `use_pct` > 90, or exclude the test entity via `linux_capacity_exceptions.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-1.1.134.

dataSources: `index=os` `sourcetype=df` from Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (per-host filesystem inventory) Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (`Splunk_TA_nix`, Splunkbase #833) with Universal Forwarder on macOS — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
index=os sourcetype=df host=*
| where MountedOn="/" OR match(MountedOn, "^/System/Volumes/Data$")
| eval use_pct=coalesce(tonumber(UsePct), tonumber(PercentUsed), round((UsedKB/SizeKB)*100,2))
| where use_pct > 90
| table _time, host, Filesystem, MountedOn, SizeKB, AvailKB, use_pct
| sort - use_pct
description: macOS endpoints exhaust `/System/Volumes/Data` quickly with local Time Machine snapshots, Xcode caches, and mail attachments. The TA `df` input already exposes per-mount utilization; scoping to root and Data volumes catches impending fullness before logging and MDM operations fail.
value: macOS endpoints exhaust `/System/Volumes/Data` quickly with local Time Machine snapshots, Xcode caches, and.... Timely UC-1.1.134 alerting on 'macOS Filesystem Capacity from Splunk TA df' reduces capacity incidents, patch regressions, and service outages before manual triage or audit channels escalate.
implementation: Enable the `df` scripted input in `Splunk_TA_nix` on macOS UF installs (Darwin is supported for many collectors). Confirm field extractions: prefer `UsePct`; if your build emits `UsedKB`/`SizeKB`, derive percent as in the SPL. Poll every 5–15 minutes. Exclude network mounts with a `where NOT match(Filesystem, "^//")` clause if noisy. Alert above 90% on `/` and `/System/Volumes/Data` (adjust for Silicon vs Intel layout).
visualization: Table (host, mount, use_pct), Line chart (use_pct trend for Data volume), Single value (count of hosts over threshold).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` avg(Performance.storage_used_percent) as used_pct
  from datamodel=Performance where nodename=Performance.Storage
  by Performance.host Performance.filesystem span=15m
| where used_pct > 90

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Patch Tuesday on `os`** — Package managers spike `host` metrics for 'macOS Filesystem Capacity from Splunk TA df'. Correlate with apt/yum logs in the same `df` window.

2. **Nightly backup I/O on `host`** — Predictable `count` burst on fixed cron; compare `_time` minute before paging.

3. **Synthetic probe on `df`** — Nagios/Zabbix polls `host` and mimics sustained load without crossing `use_pct` > 90.

4. **New host onboarding** — `host` baseline unstable first 48h after UF deploy.

**Suppression mechanism:** `linux_capacity_exceptions.csv` keyed on `host`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• `Splunk_TA_nix` deployed to the UF with `df` enabled in `inputs.conf`.
• Verify whether your TA version uses `UsePct` vs raw KB fields via Search `| head 1` on a pilot host.

Step 1 — Add lookup for allowed minimum free space per department if needed.

Step 2 — Create the search and optional CIM variant

Primary SPL (as in this UC’s `spl` field) stays on `sourcetype=df` for macOS (and Linux) full-fidelity field math.

If the same data is CIM-tagged to **Performance.Storage** with acceleration:

```spl
| tstats `summariesonly` avg(Performance.storage_used_percent) as used_pct
  from datamodel=Performance where nodename=Performance.Storage
  by Performance.host Performance.filesystem span=15m
| where used_pct > 90
```

Step 3 — Schedule alert; throttle per host to once per hour.

Step 4 — Validate by filling a test volume in a lab; compare to Finder and `diskutil apfs listSnapshots` when APFS snapshots distort free space.

Step 5 — Pair with UC-1.3.x macOS crash monitoring when disks are critically full.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (`Splunk_TA_nix`, Splunkbase #833) with Universal Forwarder on macOS — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=df into os. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`use_pct`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: We warn when a Mac’s main disk is almost full so it doesn’t freeze up or stop updating when space runs out.
